ordered_diagnoses: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath

s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging mass on the wrist with median nerve compression
salient_findings: Enlarging mass on the anterior aspect of the right wrist
Positive Phalen’s maneuver and Durkan’s test
Biphasic contrast enhancement on MRI (target sign)
key_facts: Mass located on the anterior aspect of the right wrist
Mass located along the radial edge
MRI showed a well-defined, encapsulated mass
Mass exhibited biphasic contrast enhancement (target sign)

shortlist: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath

shortlist.label: Ganglion cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of wrist mass with median nerve compression

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath
shortlist.why_kept: Typically presents as a slowly growing mass on the wrist

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause median nerve compression and has a characteristic target sign on MRI

shortlist.label: Glomus tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Can present as a painful mass on the wrist with nerve compression

shortlist.label: Nerve sheath myxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor that can cause nerve compression and has a characteristic appearance on MRI

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause nerve compression, but less likely given the MRI findings

shortlist.label: Neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause nerve compression, but less common in this location

shortlist.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare vascular tumor that can present with a similar MRI appearance

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-defined, encapsulated mass with biphasic contrast enhancement (target sign) on MRI, along with the location on the radial edge of the wrist and positive Phalen's and Durkan's tests indicating median nerve compression, are characteristic of a ganglion cyst.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath
rejected.why: While possible, the target sign on MRI is more specific for ganglion cysts

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more solid appearance on imaging and may not exhibit the target sign

rejected.label: Glomus tumor
rejected.why: Usually presents with intense pain and a distinctive blue discoloration, not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Nerve sheath myxoma
rejected.why: Less common and may not exhibit the characteristic target sign on MRI

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Does not typically cause nerve compression or exhibit the target sign on MRI

rejected.label: Neurofibroma
rejected.why: May present with multiple lesions and other systemic findings, not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
rejected.why: A rare vascular lesion that may not present with the same clinical and imaging features as described
